Replay cases omit IAM/readiness polling and unrelated caller/audit/archive experiments. ListLayers compares owned inventory across all pages, not native account page boundaries or unrelated resources; latest_filter projects only the dedicated filter layer. Runtime uses exact original ZIPs and official SDK readiness waiters.

findings.name: version-allocation
findings.statement: Identical ZIP bytes published under one name yielded versions 1, 2, 3, 4 with the same CodeSha256/CodeSize. Deleting every version then publishing identical bytes retained the layer-name counter (1 then 2), rather than restarting at 1.

findings.name: metadata-omission-and-empty
findings.statement: Omitted compatibility fields remain omitted; explicitly empty runtime/architecture arrays remain empty arrays. Omitted Description is returned as empty on publication/get; empty LicenseInfo was omitted. Version-list items omit empty Description, so do not clone publish response shapes into list items.

findings.name: version-filter-semantics
findings.statement: ListLayerVersions returns versions descending; explicit runtime/architecture filters exclude unspecified and empty metadata and combine conjunctively. Matching Python3.12/x86_64 version 2 and Node20/arm64 version 3 were observed; Python3.12+arm64 returned an empty array.

findings.name: list-layers-latest-only-filter
findings.statement: In this native capture ListLayers filtered the latest extant version, not the newest older matching version despite its LatestMatchingVersion field name: a newer Node20/arm64 version hid an older Python3.12/x86_64 version from those filtered layer lists while ListLayerVersions still returned the older match. Deleting the latest version made the older version visible again.

findings.name: pagination
findings.statement: Opaque native markers must be followed even when a filtered ListLayers page is empty: several empty pages carried NextMarker. MaxItems=1 ListLayerVersions traversed 4,3,2,1 and omitted NextMarker on the final page. Invalid markers returned native InvalidParameterValueException.

findings.name: download-byte-identity
findings.statement: GetLayerVersion by name/layer ARN and GetLayerVersionByArn returned real downloadable archives exactly identical to uploaded bytes, with matching SHA256. Signed URL capabilities are redacted, not fixtures; original ZIP/base64 bytes and response metadata are retained.

findings.name: ordered-overlay-and-attachment-boundary
findings.statement: Actual Python3.12 x86_64 imports and /opt/shared.txt showed later attached layers win overlapping paths while disjoint files merge. Five distinct layers worked; six and exact duplicate attachment were rejected without changing the already-running configuration. The duplicate error wording says different versions even for two identical ARNs.

findings.name: replacement-clearing-and-compatibility
findings.statement: Layers configuration is replacement, not merge; [] removes layer files. A pure-Python layer labeled Node20+arm64 attached to and executed in Python3.12+x86_64, so that metadata does not enforce attachment compatibility in this case. This does not establish whether mismatched native binaries would load.

findings.name: caller-not-execution-role
findings.statement: Scoped STS caller without GetLayerVersion successfully created a no-layer function, was denied direct GetLayerVersion and new attachment, and successfully updated unrelated environment on an existing attachment. A scoped caller with GetLayerVersion attached and ran the layer while the execution role explicitly denied GetLayerVersion. This locates permission checking at the deploying caller/new layer reference, not runtime execution-role fetching.

findings.name: readiness
findings.statement: Initial create attempts observed execution-role trust propagation failures before succeeding. Function State and LastUpdateStatus were polled to readiness before runtime assertions; these controls prevent interpreting eventual IAM/Lambda readiness as layer rejection.

findings.name: deletion-and-retained-consumers
findings.statement: DeleteLayerVersion present and missing both returned HTTP204. Deleted layer Get/GetByArn returned 404; new CreateFunction attachment, explicit reattachment to a current consumer, and attachment after clearing all returned InvalidParameterValueException. Existing consumers continued working, including a changed boot UUID after unrelated environment update.

findings.name: published-snapshot-cold-retention
findings.statement: Published snapshot retained layer bytes after deletion and clearing latest. The dedicated cold experiment did not invoke either function variant until after those changes: first qualified invocation still imported A from /opt while first latest invocation lacked it. This goes beyond the earlier warmed snapshot observation.

findings.name: private-version-policy
findings.statement: Own-account grant serialized literal Statement/Policy JSON strings with IAM root principal, scalar Action and Resource, policy Version=2012-10-17 and Id=default. Revisions changed on modifications; duplicate Sid returned 409, missing Sid returned 404, stale add/remove guards returned 412. Removing the last statement made policy Get return 404, not an empty Policy object.

findings.name: relative-symlink
findings.statement: Inline layer ZIP with Unix relative symlink python/link_alias.py -> link_target.py published, downloaded byte-identically, attached, and imported successfully. Runtime os.path.islink=true and os.readlink verified preservation as an actual symlink under /opt/python. No traversal or outside-root paths were used.

findings.name: duplicate-member-path
findings.statement: A layer ZIP with two central-directory entries named python/dupe.py was accepted and downloaded byte-identically; runtime import selected the last archive entry. This is separate from ordered overlays across distinct layers.

findings.name: cloudtrail-management
findings.statement: Bounded event-history lookup returned owned native layer management records, including API-version-suffixed eventName values. The artifact retains literal CloudTrailEvent strings, request IDs, parameters and recorded response omissions; read-only identity fields are redacted. This is positive audit evidence, not completeness or non-emission evidence.

limitations: CloudTrail event-history lookup is bounded to two scans, at most four 50-event pages each; absence is not evidence of non-emission. No trail was created.

No cross-account grants, public grants, organization conditions, S3-backed layers, ECR, code signing, quotas beyond six tiny attachments, provisioned concurrency, or incompatible native machine-code loading were exercised.
Execution role deliberately has no CloudWatch Logs allow; synchronous invocation payload and Tail are the runtime evidence.
No 50-MiB compressed or 250-MiB uncompressed size boundaries were probed; all archives are tiny. Do not infer size enforcement from this capture.

ListLayers result arrays preserve unrelated entries and pagination shape, but unrelated layer names/ARN name components are deterministically pseudonymized. Unrelated CloudTrail records were excluded explicitly with selection metadata.

Only safe relative in-root symlink and repeated regular-file entries were tested; no traversal, absolute symlink, cycles, directory/file conflicts, permissions escalation or outside-root extraction behavior is established.

No cross-account authorization, explicit caller Deny versus resource-policy Allow precedence, organization conditions or account quotas were explored. Caller no-read denial used absent identity Allow, with positive controls.

replay_contract.zip_encoding: artifacts[name].zip.base64 is the exact submitted ZIP; source files or ordered entries are retained beside it
replay_contract.aws_environment_dependencies: IAM execution role trust must become assumable; Lambda State=Active and LastUpdateStatus=Successful required before invokes. Signed download URLs must be regenerated, not replayed.
replay_contract.assertion_style: Compare native output field presence, semantics, bytes and errors; map generated native resource IDs, timestamps, revisions and request IDs rather than hard-coding them.
